business.title: Herpes zoster and major vascular events in a general population without prior cardiovascular event from Shizuoka Kokuho database
business.description: Herpes zoster (HZ) is associated with a risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD), but findings may differ according to baseline risk profiles. We evaluated the association between HZ and CVD among adults without prior CVD. We used a municipal-level health insurance database in Japan. Adults aged 50–84 years without prior CVD were included. HZ was defined using ICD-10 diagnostic codes with concurrent antiviral prescription. The primary outcome was a composite of unstable angina pectoris, myocardial infarction, or stroke requiring hospitalization. Propensity score matching was performed and Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs). Sensitivity analyses were conducted in individuals with Charlson Comorbidity Index ≥ 1. After propensity score matching, 94,269 individuals (20,575 HZ cases and 73,846 controls) were included. During a median follow-up of 58 months, 1,214 (1.3%) experienced the primary outcome. HZ was not significantly associated with increased risk (HR, 1.03; 95% CI, 0.90–1.18; p = 0.66). In a sensitivity analysis, HZ showed a non-significant trend toward higher risk (HR, 1.33; 95% CI, 0.90–1.96). In adults without prior CVD, HZ was not significantly associated with CVD events. However, a possible excess risk among individuals with comorbidities could not be excluded, supporting further evaluation in higher-risk populations.

science.title: Did Stonehenge's stones really come from Wales and Scotland? Fact check
science.description: Where Stonehenge's stones came from is largely measured. Many bluestones match Preseli outcrops in west Wales and the Altar Stone matches the Orcadian Basin of north-east Scotland, both Established. How they traveled is Disputed: most archaeologists say people hauled them, while some earth scientists argue for glacier ice, now challenged by a 2026 sand-grain test. Waun Mawn as an earlier circle and West Woods as the sarsen source are Disputed. The Altar Stone's route is Unverified. Giants and wizards are Fringe, and Geoffrey of Monmouth's Merlin story is medieval folklore.

science.title: Three giant black holes discovered in a galaxy from the dawn of time
science.description: Astronomers have discovered three actively feeding black holes inside a single galaxy more than 12.5 billion light-years away, revealing a remarkable scene from the universe’s infancy. Two of the black holes are separated by just 620 light-years and are expected to eventually merge, while a third lurks farther away. One weighs an astonishing 80 million suns, and another is growing faster than conventional theories predict.

science.title: Agricultural chemical intensification and ecological footprint comparative analysis of pesticide and insecticide consumption
science.description: This study examines how agricultural chemical intensification affects environmental sustainability in Nigeria by comparing the ecological footprint impacts of pesticide and insecticide consumption from 1990 to 2024. The analysis incorporates economic growth, renewable energy consumption, financial development, and energy use as control variables, and tests the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis. To capture nonlinearities and gradual structural shifts, the study uses the BDS nonlinearity test, Fourier-augmented unit root procedures, the Fourier Bootstrap ARDL approach for long-run estimation, and the Fourier Toda–Yamamoto causality framework. The empirical results reveal that both pesticide and insecticide consumption are positively and significantly associated with Nigeria’s ecological footprint in the long run, consistent with chemical intensification contributing to environmental pressure. Renewable energy consumption reduces ecological pressure, whereas financial development exhibits mixed effects. The results are consistent with an inverted-U relationship, although the evidence is weaker for some specifications. Fourier Toda–Yamamoto results indicate predictive causality between chemical use and ecological footprint in both directions, with the INSECT → EF link strongest at the 5% level and the others significant at the 10% level. The study suggests that Nigeria’s input-intensive agricultural growth pattern is environmentally unsustainable and underscores the need for cleaner energy systems, sustainable agricultural practices, and environmentally aligned financial development. The findings provide policy insights for balancing agricultural productivity and ecological sustainability in developing economies.

science.title: Inhibitors for a conserved filarial catechol-O-methyltransferase with potent efficacy against all life-stages of Brugia malayi infection in gerbils
science.description: Filarial nematodes of genus Brugia cause lymphatic filariasis, with over 36 million chronically debilitated people and 885 million at risk in Asia and sub-Saharan Africa. Current drugs have limited efficacy. Herein, we unveil a unique catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT) called BmMT that is conserved in filarial nematodes with a lethal RNAi phenotype in Caenorhabditis elegans and lacks orthologs in mammals. COMTs catabolize catecholamines that if left to accumulate are lethal in nematodes. BmMT possesses core structural and functional features of COMTs, but is divergent from mammalian COMTs. Three inhibitors of BmMT (NSC177383, NSC133100, and NSC56410) depicted potent activity against all life-stages of B. malayi. The inhibitors bind within BmMT’s catechol substrate-binding fold with high occupancy (> 80%) of residues, implying they block catecholamine binding. As proof of principle for the mode of action of BmMT inhibitors, treatment of B. malayi worms with NSC56410 elevated catecholamines, consistent with observations using morpholino-mediated knockdown of BmMT. Importantly, treatment of B. malayi-infected gerbils with NSC133100 (100 mg/kg/day) or NSC56410 (10 mg/kg/day) almost completely eliminated all microfilariae and adult worms. Together, these studies unveil BmMT as a promising new molecular target, with its selective inhibitors as optimizable lead-compounds for the development of novel efficacious antifilarial drugs.
